cohort: The study included 410 women who delivered at Rwinkwavu District Hospital in the Eastern Province of Rwanda.
finding: The prevalence of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) was 15.1%, and marital status, mode of delivery, labor induction, and prolonged labor were significantly associated with it.
mod_finding: Women who delivered by Cesarean section were 3.092 times more likely to suffer from PPH compared to those who delivered vaginally.
cross-section timing: At the time of or shortly after delivery, during hospital stay.
